params.question: The WHO's 2030 cervical cancer elimination strategy sets a target of screening 90 per cent of women with a high-performance test by age 35 and again by 45.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The screening target is actually 70 per cent, not 90 per cent. The WHO 2030 targets follow a 90-70-90 pattern: 90% HPV vaccination by age 15, 70% screening by ages 35 and 45, and 90% treatment of identified disease. Only vaccination and treatment carry the 90% target.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the screening target is 70 per cent, not 90 per cent. The three 2030 targets are: 90% of girls fully vaccinated against HPV by age 15, 70% of women screened by ages 35 and 45, and 90% of women with cervical disease receiving treatment. Remember the pattern as 90-70-90.

interactions.label: A 28-year-old woman on combined oral contraceptives has a reddish, velvety, gran

params.question: A 28-year-old woman on combined oral contraceptives has a reddish, velvety, granular area around the external os on speculum examination. The cervix is smooth and non-indurated. Which benign cervical lesion does this most likely represent?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nabothian cysts appear as smooth, yellowish, translucent domes caused by blocked endocervical gland ducts. They do not produce a diffuse reddish, velvety area.

Correct. Ectropion (ectopy) is eversion of columnar epithelium onto the ectocervix, giving a reddish, velvety, granular appearance around the os. It is physiological with combined oral contraceptives because oestrogen drives it. The smooth, non-indurated texture rules out malignancy.
Cervical polyps are soft, reddish, pedunculated growths visible through the external os. They are discrete masses, not a diffuse granular area around the os.

Chlamydial cervicitis can mimic ectropion on inspection, but the clinical context — OC use, typical velvety granular appearance, and absence of discharge or tenderness — favours ectropion. Cervicitis must be ruled out microbiologically before treating any cervical lesion with cryotherapy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the distinguishing features: ectropion = reddish velvety area (oestrogen-driven), nabothian cysts = yellowish translucent domes, polyps = pedunculated growths, cervicitis = infectious aetiology needing microbiological confirmation.

Well done. Ectropion is the most common benign finding on the young cervix, especially with oestrogen-driven states such as OC use, pregnancy, and adolescence. Recognising it prevents unnecessary biopsy.

interactions.label: A 45-year-old woman has a 5 cm cauliflower-shaped cervical growth that bleeds on

params.question: A 45-year-old woman has a 5 cm cauliflower-shaped cervical growth that bleeds on touch. On bimanual examination, the right parametrium is indurated and extends to the pelvic side wall; the lower vagina is uninvolved. Which examination finding most reliably distinguishes locally advanced from early-stage cervical cancer?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tumour size contributes to staging but does not by itself distinguish locally advanced disease. A 5 cm tumour confined to the cervix is still early-stage if the parametrium is free.
Contact bleeding occurs in both early and advanced cervical cancer because the tumour surface is friable. It indicates malignancy but does not differentiate stage.

answers.text: Parametrial induration extending to the pelvic side wall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Feeling the parametrium for induration — that cobblestone-like hardness — is the key clinical manoeuvre. Extension to the pelvic side wall separates locally advanced disease (Stage IIIB) from disease confined near the cervix.

Discharge progressing from watery to foul-smelling reflects tumour necrosis and infection, but it is not a reliable staging criterion. Parametrial assessment on bimanual examination is what determines local extent.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key point from the narration is that feeling the parametrium for induration is what separates disease confined near the cervix from disease reaching the pelvic side wall. This is the most reliable clinical staging manoeuvre.
Exactly right. Parametrial assessment by bimanual and rectovaginal examination remains the cornerstone of clinical staging, even in centres with imaging access.

interactions.label: A 58-year-old woman with obesity and type 2 diabetes, not on hormone replacement

params.question: A 58-year-old woman with obesity and type 2 diabetes, not on hormone replacement therapy, presents with vaginal bleeding five years after her last menstrual period. What is the most appropriate initial clinical assumption?

answers.text: The bleeding is most likely atrophic vaginitis given her age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Atrophic vaginitis is common after menopause, but the clinical rule is clear: postmenopausal bleeding must be treated as endometrial cancer until proven otherwise. Obesity and diabetes further raise her risk.

answers.text: Postmenopausal bleeding must be treated as endometrial cancer until proven otherwise

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Any vaginal bleeding more than 12 months after the last period, in a woman not on HRT, must be assumed to be endometrial cancer until tissue sampling proves otherwise. In this patient, obesity and diabetes are additional risk factors that heighten suspicion.

answers.text: A cervical Pap smear is sufficient to exclude malignancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pap smears screen for cervical pathology, not endometrial disease. Endometrial cancer requires imaging (transvaginal ultrasound) and tissue sampling (endometrial biopsy or hysteroscopy-guided curettage) for diagnosis.

answers.text: Reassurance is appropriate since the probability of cancer is only ten to fifteen per cent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While the overall probability of cancer in unselected PMB populations is 10–15%, this risk climbs sharply with age, obesity, diabetes, and nulliparity — all present here. The safe clinical rule is to assume cancer until proven otherwise.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the critical clinical rule: postmenopausal bleeding (>12 months after last period, not on HRT) = endometrial cancer until proven otherwise. Examination alone never confirms the diagnosis; imaging and tissue sampling are essential.
Well done. PMB accounts for about 90% of endometrial cancer presentations, and this early symptom is why endometrial cancer is usually caught at a treatable stage.

interactions.label: Which of the following is considered a protective factor against ovarian cancer,

params.question: Which of the following is considered a protective factor against ovarian cancer, and what mechanism does it share with other protective factors?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nulliparity actually increases ovarian cancer risk. Each pregnancy suppresses ovulation for nine months; nulliparous women have more lifetime ovulatory cycles and therefore more repeated ovarian surface repair episodes.
Early menarche increases the total number of ovulatory cycles across a lifetime, raising rather than lowering ovarian cancer risk.

Correct. OC pills suppress ovulation, reducing repeated wounding and repair of the ovarian surface epithelium. This ovulation-suppression mechanism is shared by multiparity, breastfeeding, and tubal ligation — all of which reduce ovarian cancer risk.

answers.text: Hormone replacement therapy — stabilises the ovarian epithelium

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HRT increases ovarian cancer risk. It does not suppress ovulation (which has already ceased after menopause) and may promote epithelial proliferation through exogenous oestrogen.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key concept is the ovulation theory: each ovulation wounds the ovarian surface, and repeated repair drives malignant change. Factors that suppress ovulation (OC pills, multiparity, breastfeeding, tubal ligation) are protective; factors that increase lifetime ovulations (nulliparity, early menarche, late menopause) raise risk.

Exactly. The unifying mechanism behind OC pills, multiparity, breastfeeding, and tubal ligation as protective factors is ovulation suppression — fewer ovulatory cycles means less repeated wounding and repair of the ovarian surface.

interactions.label: A 24-year-old woman presents at 10 weeks of gestation with severe vomiting, a ut

params.question: A 24-year-old woman presents at 10 weeks of gestation with severe vomiting, a uterus larger than expected for dates, vaginal bleeding, and passage of grape-like vesicles. Her serum β-hCG is markedly elevated. Which clinical finding is pathognomonic for a complete hydatidiform mole?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hyperemesis occurs because very high β-hCG cross-reacts with TSH receptors, but it is a feature of many conditions including normal twin pregnancy. It is characteristic but not pathognomonic for a molar pregnancy.
A large-for-dates uterus can also be seen in multiple pregnancy, uterine fibroids, or incorrect dating. It raises suspicion but is not pathognomonic.

Correct. The narration describes passage of grape-like vesicles as pathognomonic for a complete hydatidiform mole. These vesicles are swollen chorionic villi, and their passage clinches the clinical diagnosis even before histology.

Very high β-hCG is characteristic of molar pregnancy but is not pathognomonic — it can also occur in multiple gestations and choriocarcinoma. The pathognomonic finding is the passage of grape-like vesicles.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember that pathognomonic means the finding is unique to this condition. Passage of grape-like vesicles (swollen chorionic villi) is seen only in complete hydatidiform moles. The other findings — hyperemesis, large uterus, and elevated β-hCG — are characteristic but can occur in other conditions as well.

Well done. While hyperemesis, large-for-dates uterus, and elevated β-hCG all raise suspicion, passage of grape-like vesicles is the only pathognomonic clinical finding for a complete hydatidiform mole.
